list of sessions\n        [  # list of trials for session 1\n            neuron_by_time_matrix,  # shape: (n_neurons, n_timepoints)\n            neuron_by_time_matrix,  # trial 2\n            ...\n        ],\n        [  # list of trials for session 2\n            ...\n        ],\n        ...\n    ],\n\n    'input': [  # list of sessions\n        [  # list of trials for session 1\n            input_data,  # stimulus/task variables, shape: (n_input, n_timepoints) or (n_input)\n            ...\n        ],\n        ...\n    ],\n\n    'output': [  # list of sessions\n        [  # list of trials for session 1\n            output_data,  # behavioral response, shape (n_output, n_timepoints) or (n_output)\n            ...\n        ],\n        ...\n    ],\n\n    'subjects': list of str, # ids of all subjects, length n_subjects\n    'subject_idx': shape (n_sessions,), # index into subjects for each session\n\n    'brain_regions': list of str, # names of the brain regions recorded from, e.g. ALM, V1\n    'brain_region_idx': [ # list of sessions\n        neuron_region_idx, # shape: (n_neurons,)\n    ] # index into `brain_regions` for each neuron\n\n    'input_names': list of str, # names for each input, of length n_input\n    'output_names': list of str, # names of each output, of length n_output\n    'output_values': [ # list of length n_output\n        [ output_val0, ... ], # list of str of length d_output[0], name of each output value\n        ...\n    ],\n\n    'metadata': {\n        'task_description': str, # description of output tasks\n        'time_bin_size': float, # length of time bin in ms\n        'temporal_alignment_event': str, # description of alignment event\n        'off_start': float or None, # They could be task inputs to the animal, but inputs to the animal can also be decoder outputs.\n  - Examples: time from an aligning signal, stimulus characteristics, our animal behavior such as:\n    - visual: contrast, position, orientation\n    - audio: frequency, amplitude\n    - behavior: running speed, pupil size\n  - Dimensions: (d_input, n_timepoints) for each trial. \n  - Should capture all relevant contextual information for the decoder\n  - If an input is a time such as onset of some stimulus, represent it as a binary time series. \n\n- **output**: Variables to be decoded/predicted from neural activity\n  - These are what we want the decoder to **predict**. They could be the animal's output behavior or properties of the stimulus.\n  - Output variables must be **categorical**, i.e. discrete rather than continuous. If a variable is not discrete, follow instructions from Decoder Task to discretize it. \n  - Examples: stimulus properties (contrast, orientation), choice (left/right), reaction time, position\n  - Can be time-varying or discrete values per trial. If at all possible, make it time-varying\n  - If an output is a time such as when a behavior occurred, represent it as a binary time series. \n\n- **subjects**: List of names of all unique subjects (mice).\n- **subject_idx**: Index into subjects for each session.\n  - Order should match order of sessions in `neural`, etc.\n\n- **brain_regions**: List of names of all brain regions recorded from.\n- **brain_region_idx**: Index into brain_regions for each neuron in each session.\n\n- **input_names**: Names of each input variable.\n  - Order should match order of `input` dimensions. \n\n- **output_names**: Names of each output variable.\n  - Order should match order of `output` dimensions.\n- **output_values**: Names of each output value for each output variable.\n  - Order should match categorical `output` values.\n\n- **metadata**: Descriptive information. \n  - `task_description`: Concise description of the task\n  - `temporal_alignment_event`: Concise description of temporal alignment event\n  - `off_start`: Signed time from alignment event to start of trial. Negative means before event, positive after. \n  - `off_end`: Signed time from alignment event to end of trial\n  - Add other relevant fields, e.g. `session_info`\n\n## Python environment\n\n- All required Python packages are already installed in the system Python environment.\n- Use `python3` to run any python code.\n- If you need to install additional libraries, use `pip install`.\n\n## Decoder Reference\n\n- Run this script with `python train_decoder.py <data_file_path>` to validate.\n- Optional arguments:\n  - `--verify-only`: Only verify data format and print summary, then exit (does not train decoder).\n  - `--plot-samples`: Plot sample trials from data and save to png files.\n  - `--cpu`: Force torch to use CPU only (use if GPU runs out of memory).\n- Pipe the output to the designated file so that the user can examine it.\n\n### Purpose\n\nThese functions will be used during the validation phase to ensure:\n1. = vid_file_offset - bit_start\n   335→    except Exception:\n   336→        pass\n   337→\n   338→    clu_refs = obj['clu'][()].flatten()\n   339→    all_spike_times = []\n   340→    all_spike_trials = []\n   341→    all_qualities = []\n   342→\n   343→    for probe_num in probes:\n   344→        probe_idx = probe_num - 1\n   345→        probe_ref = clu_refs[probe_idx]\n   346→        probe_group = f[probe_ref]\n   347→        quality_refs = probe_group['quality'][()].flatten()\n   348→        trialtm_refs = probe_group['trialtm'][()].flatten()\n   349→        trial_refs = probe_group['trial'][()].flatten()\n   350→\n   351→        for i in range(len(quality_refs)):\n   352→            quality = h5_read_string(f, quality_refs[i]).strip().lower()\n   353→            trialtm = f[trialtm_refs[i]][()].flatten().astype(np.float64)\n   354→            trial = f[trial_refs[i]][()].flatten().astype(np.float64)\n   355→            all_qualities.append(quality)\n   356→            all_spike_times.append(trialtm)\n   357→            all_spike_trials.append(trial)\n   358→\n   359→    # --- traj ---\n   360→    traj_data = None\n   361→    try:\n   362→        traj_refs = obj['traj'][()].flatten()\n   363→        traj_data = {'views': []}\n   364→        for view_idx in range(len(traj_refs)):\n   365→            traj_group = f[traj_refs[view_idx]]\n   366→            ts_refs = traj_group['ts'][()].flatten()\n   367→            ft_refs = traj_group['frameTimes'][()].flatten()\n   368→            feat_names_refs = traj_group['featNames'][()].flatten()\n   369→\n   370→            # Read feat names from first trial\n   371→            feat_refs_trial = f[feat_names_refs[0]][()].flatten()\n   372→            feat_names = [h5_read_string(f, fr) for fr in feat_refs_trial]\n   373→\n   374→            view_trials = []\n   375→            for t in range(min(ntrials, len(ts_refs))):\n   376→                try:\n   377→                    ts = f[ts_refs[t]][()].astype(np.float64)  # (nFeats, 3, nFrames) in HDF5\n   378→                    ft = f[ft_refs[t]][()].flatten().astype(np.float64)\n   379→                    view_trials.append({'ts': ts, 'frameTimes': ft, 'ts_format': 'hdf5'})\n   380→                except Exception:\n   381→                    view_trials.append(None)\n   382→            traj_data['views'].append({'trials': view_trials, 'feat_names': feat_names})\n   383→    except Exception:\n   384→        pass\n   385→\n   386→    f.close()\n   387→\n   388→    return {\n   389→        'bp': bp, 'vidshift': vidshift, 'ntrials': ntrials,\n   390→        'all_spike_times': all_spike_times, 'all_spike_trials': all_spike_trials,\n   391→        'all_qualities': all_qualities, 'traj_data': traj_data,\n   392→        'n_units_raw': len(all_qualities),\n   393→    }\n   394→\n   395→\n   396→def load_session(anm, date, probes, data_dir_key, params):\n   397→    \"\"\"\n   398→    Load and process one session, following the reference pipeline:\n   399→    loadObjs -> findClusters -> alignSpikes -> getSeq -> removeLowFRClusters\n   400→    Also loads motion energy and computes kinematic features.\n   401→    \"\"\"\n   402→    t0 = time.time()\n   403→    data_dir = DATA_DIRS[data_dir_key]\n   404→    data_fn = os.path.join(data_dir, f'data_structure_{anm}_{date}.mat')\n   405→    me_fn = os.path.join(data_dir, f'motionEnergy_{anm}_{date}.mat')\n   406→\n   407→    session_id = f'{anm}_{date}'\n   408→\n   409→    if not os.path.exists(data_fn):\n   410→        print(f\"  WARNING: {data_fn} not found, skipping\")\n   411→        return None\n   412→\n   413→    # Detect format and load raw data\n   414→    fmt = _detect_file_format(data_fn)\n   415→    try:\n   416→        if fmt == 'hdf5':\n   417→            raw = _load_raw_data_hdf5(data_fn, probes)\n   418→        else:\n   419→            raw = _load_raw_data_v5(data_fn, probes)\n   420→    except Exception as e:\n   421→        print(f\"  WARNING: Could not load {session_id}: {e}\")\n   422→        return None\n   423→\n   424→    bp = raw['bp']\n   425→    ntrials = raw['ntrials']\n   426→    vidshift = raw['vidshift']\n   427→    all_spike_times = raw['all_spike_times']\n   428→    all_spike_trials = raw['all_spike_trials']\n   429→    all_qualities = raw['all_qualities']\n   430→    traj_data = raw['traj_data']\n   431→    n_units_before_quality = raw['n_units_raw']\n   432→    ev = bp['ev']\n   433→\n   434→    # --- Filter clusters by quality ---\n   435→    quality_exclude = params['quality_exclude']\n   436→    keep_mask = np.array([q not in quality_exclude and q != '' and q != 'nan'\n   437→                          for q in all_qualities])\n   438→    good_indices = np.where(keep_mask)[0]\n   439→\n   440→    if len(good_indices) == 0:\n   441→        print(f\"  WARNING: {session_id} has no units after quality filter, skipping\")\n   442→        return None\n   443→\n   444→    # --- Trial filtering ---\n   445→    trial_mask = (bp['early'] == 0) & (bp['stim_enable'] == 0)\n   446→    valid_trials = np.where(trial_mask)[0] + 1  # 1-indexed\n   447→    if len(valid_trials) < 2:\n   448→        print(f\"  WARNING: {session_id} has < 2 valid trials, skipping\")\n   449→        return None\n   450→\n   451→    # --- Align spikes to goCue and bin ---\n   452→    align_times = ev[params['align_event']]\n   453→    edges = np.arange(params['tmin'], params['tmax'] + params['dt'], params['dt'])\n   454→    time_axis = edges[:-1] + params['dt'] / 2\n   455→    n_timebins = len(time_axis)\n   456→    n_valid_trials = len(valid_trials)\n   457→\n   458→    trialdat = np.zeros((len(good_indices), n_timebins, n_valid_trials), dtype=np.float32)\n   459→\n   460→    for neuron_idx, clu_idx in enumerate(good_indices):\n   461→        spike_tm = all_spike_times[clu_idx]\n   462→        spike_trial = all_spike_trials[clu_idx]\n   463→\n   464→        for t_idx, trial_num in enumerate(valid_trials):\n   465→            spk_mask = spike_trial == trial_num\n   466→            if not np.any(spk_mask):\n   467→                continue\n   468→            spk_times = spike_tm[spk_mask] - align_times[trial_num - 1]\n   469→            counts, _ = np.histogram(spk_times, bins=edges)\n   470→            fr = causal_gaussian_smooth(counts.astype(np.float64) / params['dt'],\n   471→                                       params['smooth_window'],\n   472→                                       params['smooth_bctype'])\n   473→            trialdat[neuron_idx, :, t_idx] = fr.astype(np.float32)\n   474→\n   475→    # --- Remove low FR clusters ---\n   476→    mean_fr = np.mean(trialdat, axis=(1, 2))\n   477→    fr_mask = mean_fr > params['low_fr']\n   478→    trialdat = trialdat[fr_mask, :, :]\n   479→    n_neurons = trialdat.shape[0]\n   480→\n   481→    if n_neurons < params['min_units']:\n   482→        print(f\"  WARNING: {session_id} has {n_neurons} units (< {params['min_units']}), skipping\")\n   483→        return None\n   484→\n   485→    # --- Extract trial-level variables ---\n   486→    valid_trial_indices = valid_trials - 1\n   487→    lick_direction = bp['R'][valid_trial_indices].copy()\n   488→    behavioral_context = 1.0 - bp['autowater'][valid_trial_indices]\n   489→    outcome = bp['hit'][valid_trial_indices].copy()\n   490→\n   491→    # --- Load Motion Energy ---\n   492→    me_data = None\n   493→    if os.path.exists(me_fn):\n   494→        try:\n   495→            me_data = _load_motion_energy_generic(me_fn, traj_data, vidshift,\n   496→                                                  align_times, time_axis, ntrials)\n   497→        except Exception as e:\n   498→            print(f\"  WARNING: Could not load motion energy for {session_id}: {e}\")\n   499→\n   500→    # --- Compute tongue and paw velocity from DLC ---\n   501→    tongue_vel = _compute_feature_velocity_generic(\n   502→        traj_data, ntrials, view=2, feat_name='top_tongue',\n   503→        vidshift=vidshift, align_times=align_times,\n   504→        time_axis=time_axis, is_tongue=True)\n   505→\n   506→    paw_vel = _compute_feature_velocity_generic(\n   507→        traj_data, ntrials, view=2, feat_name='top_paw',\n   508→        vidshift=vidshift, align_times=align_times,\n   509→        time_axis=time_axis, is_tongue=False)\n   510→\n   511→    # --- Subsample to valid trials ---\n   512→    valid_0idx = valid_trial_indices  # 0-indexed\n   513→\n   514→    if tongue_vel is not None:\n   515→        tongue_vel = tongue_vel[:, valid_0idx]\n   516→    if paw_vel is not None:\n   517→        paw_vel = paw_vel[:, valid_0idx]\n   518→    if me_data is not None:\n   519→        me_data = me_data[:, valid_0idx]\n   520→\n   521→    # --- Discretize continuous outputs (50th percentile per session) ---\n   522→    tongue_vel_disc = _discretize_velocity(tongue_vel, n_timebins, n_valid_trials)\n   523→    paw_vel_disc = _discretize_velocity(paw_vel, n_timebins, n_valid_trials)\n   524→    me_disc = _discretize_velocity(me_data, n_timebins, n_valid_trials)\n   525→\n   526→    elapsed = time.time() - t0\n   527→    print(f\"  {session_id}: {n_neurons} neurons, {n_valid_trials} trials, \"\n   528→          f\"{n_units_before_quality} raw units -> {int(keep_mask.sum())} after quality -> \"\n   529→          f\"{n_neurons} after FR filter ({elapsed:.1f}s)\")\n   530→\n   531→    return {\n   532→        'session_id': session_id,\n   533→        'animal': anm,\n   534→        'date': date,\n   535→        'n_neurons': n_neurons,\n   536→        'n_trials': n_valid_trials,\n   537→        'time_axis': time_axis,\n   538→        'trialdat': trialdat,  # (n_neurons, n_timebins, n_trials)\n   539→        'lick_direction': lick_direction,\n   540→        'behavioral_context': behavioral_context,\n   541→        'outcome': outcome,\n   542→        'tongue_vel_disc': tongue_vel_disc,  # (n_timebins, n_trials)\n   543→        'paw_vel_disc': paw_vel_disc,\n   544→        'me_disc': me_disc,\n   545→        'tongue_vel_raw': tongue_vel,\n   546→        'paw_vel_raw': paw_vel,\n   547→        'me_raw': me_data,\n   548→    }\n   549→\n   550→\n   551→def _load_motion_energy_generic(me_fn, traj_data, vidshift, align_times, time_axis, ntrials):\n   552→    \"\"\"Load motion energy and align to neural time axis following loadMotionEnergy.m\"\"\"\n   553→    import scipy.io as sio\n   554→\n   555→    me_cell = None\n   556→    try:\n   557→        me_file = sio.loadmat(me_fn, squeeze_me=True)\n   558→        me_struct = me_file['me']\n   559→        me_cell = me_struct['data'].item()\n   560→    except Exception:\n   561→        me_h5 = h5py.File(me_fn, 'r')\n   562→        me_grp = me_h5['me']\n   563→        me_data_refs = me_grp['data'][()].flatten()\n   564→        me_cell = [me_h5[ref][()].flatten().astype(np.float64) for ref in me_data_refs]\n   565→        me_h5.close()\n   566→\n   567→    side_cam = traj_data['views'][0] if traj_data is not None else None\n   568→    n_time = len(time_axis)\n   569→    me_aligned = np.full((n_time, ntrials), np.nan, dtype=np.float32)\n   570→\n   571→    for trix in range(ntrials):\n   572→        try:\n   573→            me_trial = me_cell[trix].flatten().astype(np.float64) if hasattr(me_cell[trix], 'flatten') else np.array([float(me_cell[trix])])\n   574→        except (IndexError, TypeError):\n   575→            continue\n   576→        if me_trial.size == 0:\n   577→            continue\n   578→\n   579→        ft = None\n   580→        if side_cam is not None and trix < len(side_cam['trials']) and side_cam['trials'][trix] is not None:\n   581→            ft = side_cam['trials'][trix]['frameTimes']\n   582→        if ft is None or ft.size == 0 or np.all(np.isnan(ft)):\n   583→            ft = np.arange(1, me_trial.size + 1) / 400.0\n   584→\n   585→        ft_aligned = ft - vidshift - align_times[trix]\n   586→        min_len = min(len(ft_aligned), len(me_trial))\n   587→        ft_aligned, me_trial = ft_aligned[:min_len], me_trial[:min_len]\n   588→        valid = ~np.isnan(ft_aligned) & ~np.isnan(me_trial)\n   589→        if valid.sum() < 2:\n   590→            continue\n   591→        try:\n   592→            me_aligned[:, trix] = interp1d(ft_aligned[valid], me_trial[valid],\n   593→                                           kind='linear', bounds_error=False,\n   594→                                           fill_value=np.nan)(time_axis).astype(np.float32)\n   595→        except Exception:\n   596→            continue\n   597→\n   598→    for trix in range(ntrials):\n   599→        col = me_aligned[:, trix]\n   600→        if not np.isnan(col).all() and np.isnan(col).any():\n   601→            me_aligned[:, trix] = _fill_nearest(col)\n   602→\n   603→    return me_aligned\n   604→\n   605→\n   606→def _compute_feature_velocity_generic(traj_data, ntrials, view, feat_name, vidshift, align_times, time_axis, is_tongue=False):\n   607→    \"\"\"Compute velocity of a DLC feature from traj_data (format-agnostic).\"\"\"\n   608→    n_time = len(time_axis)\n   609→    speed = np.full((n_time, ntrials), np.nan, dtype=np.float32)\n   610→\n   611→    if traj_data is None:\n   612→        return None\n   613→\n   614→    view_idx = view - 1\n   615→    if view_idx >= len(traj_data['views']):\n   616→        return None\n   617→\n   618→    view_data = traj_data['views'][view_idx]\n   619→    feat_names = view_data['feat_names']\n   620→\n   621→    feat_idx = None\n   622→    for idx, fn in enumerate(feat_names):\n   623→        if fn == feat_name:\n   624→            feat_idx = idx\n   625→            break\n   626→    if feat_idx is None:\n   627→        for idx, fn in enumerate(feat_names):\n   628→            if feat_name in fn:\n   629→                feat_idx = idx\n   630→                break\n   631→    if feat_idx is None:\n   632→        return None\n   633→\n   634→    for trix in range(min(ntrials, len(view_data['trials']))):\n   635→        trial_info = view_data['trials'][trix]\n   636→        if trial_info is None:\n   637→            continue\n   638→        try:\n   639→            ts = trial_info['ts']\n   640→            ft = trial_info['frameTimes']\n   641→            ts_fmt = trial_info['ts_format']\n   642→\n   643→            if ts.ndim != 3:\n   644→                continue\n   645→\n   646→            if ts_fmt == 'hdf5':\n   647→                x_raw = ts[feat_idx, 0, :]\n   648→                y_raw = ts[feat_idx, 1, :]\n   649→            else:\n   650→                x_raw = ts[:, 0, feat_idx]\n   651→                y_raw = ts[:, 1, feat_idx]\n   652→\n   653→            if ft.size == 0 or np.all(np.isnan(ft)):\n   654→                ft = np.arange(1, len(x_raw) + 1) / 400.0\n   655→\n   656→            ft_aligned = ft - vidshift - align_times[trix]\n   657→            min_len = min(len(ft_aligned), len(x_raw))\n   658→            ft_a, x_r, y_r = ft_aligned[:min_len], x_raw[:min_len], y_raw[:min_len]\n   659→\n   660→            valid = ~np.isnan(ft_a) & ~np.isnan(x_r) & ~np.isnan(y_r)\n   661→            if valid.sum() < 2:\n   662→                continue\n   663→\n   664→            xpos = interp1d(ft_a[valid], x_r[valid], kind='linear',\n   665→                            bounds_error=False, fill_value=np.nan)(time_axis)\n   666→            ypos = interp1d(ft_a[valid], y_r[valid], kind='linear',\n   667→                            bounds_error=False, fill_value=np.nan)(time_axis)\n   668→\n   669→            if not is_tongue:\n   670→                xpos = _fill_nearest(xpos)\n   671→                ypos = _fill_nearest(ypos)\n   672→\n   673→            xvel = np.gradient(xpos)\n   674→            yvel = np.gradient(ypos)\n   675→\n   676→            if is_tongue:\n   677→                xvel[np.isnan(xvel)] = 0\n   678→                yvel[np.isnan(yvel)] = 0\n   679→            else:\n   680→                base_xvel = np.nanmedian(np.diff(xpos))\n   681→                base_yvel = np.nanmedian(np.diff(ypos))\n   682→                xvel -= (base_xvel if not np.isnan(base_xvel) else 0)\n   683→                yvel -= (base_yvel if not np.isnan(base_yvel) else 0)\n   684→                xvel = _fill_nearest(xvel)\n   685→                yvel = _fill_nearest(yvel)\n   686→\n   687→            speed[:, trix] = np.sqrt(xvel**2 + yvel**2).astype(np.float32)\n   688→        except Exception:\n   689→            continue\n   690→\n   691→    return speed\n   692→\n   693→\n   694→def _fill_nearest(arr):\n   695→    \"\"\"Fill NaN values with nearest non-NaN value.\"\"\"\n   696→    nans = np.isnan(arr)\n   697→    if not nans.any():\n   698→        return arr\n   699→    if nans.all():\n   700→        return arr\n   701→    valid_idx = np.where(~nans)[0]\n   702→    nan_idx = np.where(nans)[0]\n   703→    nearest = np.searchsorted(valid_idx, nan_idx).clip(0, len(valid_idx) - 1)\n   704→    arr[nans] = arr[valid_idx[nearest]]\n   705→    return arr\n   706→\n   707→\n   708→def _discretize_velocity(data, n_timebins, n_trials):\n   709→    \"\"\"Discretize continuous data into 2 bins using 50th percentile per session.\"\"\"\n   710→    if data is None:\n   711→        return np.zeros((n_timebins, n_trials), dtype=np.int64)\n   712→\n   713→    # Compute 50th percentile across all valid (non-NaN) values\n   714→    valid_vals = data[~np.isnan(data)]\n   715→    if valid_vals.size == 0:\n   716→        return np.zeros((n_timebins, n_trials), dtype=np.int64)\n   717→\n   718→    threshold = np.percentile(valid_vals, 50)\n   719→    disc = (data >= threshold).astype(np.int64)\n   720→    # Replace NaN entries with 0\n   721→    disc[np.isnan(data)] = 0\n   722→    return disc\n   723→\n   724→\n   725→# =============================================================================\n   726→# Plotting functions\n   727→# =============================================================================\n   728→\n   729→def plot_processing(session_data, save_path):\n   730→    \"\"\"Plot 738→\n   739→    # Pick a sample trial\n   740→    trial_idx = min(5, n_trials - 1)\n   741→\n   742→    # 1. --- traj (for velocity computation) ---\n    traj_data = None\n    try:\n        traj_raw = obj['traj'][0, 0]\n        traj_data = {'views': []}\n        for view_idx in range(traj_raw.shape[1]):\n            view_data = traj_raw[0, view_idx]\n            view_trials = []\n            feat_names = None\n            for t in range(min(ntrials, view_data.shape[1] if view_data.ndim > 1 else view_data.shape[0])):\n                trial_data = view_data[0, t] if view_data.ndim > 1 else view_data[t]\n                ts = trial_data['ts'].astype(np.float64)  # (nFrames, 3, nFeats) in v5\n                ft = trial_data['frameTimes'].flatten().astype(np.float64)\n                if feat_names is None:\n                    fn_raw = trial_data['featNames'].flatten()\n                    feat_names = [str(x.flat[0]).strip() for x in fn_raw]\n                view_trials.append({'ts': ts, 'frameTimes': ft, 'ts_format': 'v5'})\n            traj_data['views'].append({'trials': view_trials, 'feat_names': feat_names})\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n\n    return {\n        'bp': bp, 'vidshift': vidshift, 'ntrials': ntrials,\n        'all_spike_times': all_spike_times, 'all_spike_trials': all_spike_trials,\n        'all_qualities': all_qualities, 'traj_data': traj_data,\n        'n_units_raw': len(all_qualities),\n    }\n\n\ndef _load_raw_data_hdf5(data_fn, probes):\n    \"\"\"Load raw data from HDF5 (v7.3) format file. Returns common dict format.\"\"\"\n    f = h5py.File(data_fn, 'r')\n    obj = f['obj']\n\n    bp = {}\n    bp_group = obj['bp']\n    bp['Ntrials'] = int(bp_group['Ntrials'][()].flat[0])\n    ntrials = bp['Ntrials']\n\n    for field in ['hit', 'miss', 'no', 'early', 'L', 'R', 'autowater']:\n        bp[field] = bp_group[field][()].flatten().astype(np.float64)[:ntrials]\n\n    stim_enable = np.zeros(ntrials)\n    if 'stim' in bp_group:\n        stim_grp = bp_group['stim']\n        if 'enable' in stim_grp:\n            stim_enable = stim_grp['enable'][()].flatten().astype(np.float64)[:ntrials]\n    bp['stim_enable'] = stim_enable\n\n    ev = {}\n    ev_group = bp_group['ev']\n    for field in ['goCue', 'sample', 'delay']:\n        ev[field] = ev_group[field][()].flatten().astype(np.float64)[:ntrials]\n    bp['ev'] = ev\n\n    vidshift = 0.5\n    try:\n        bit_start = np.nanmedian(bp_group['ev']['bitStart'][()].flatten())\n        sglx = obj['sglx']\n        fs = sglx['fs'][()].flat[0]\n        bitcode_bitstart = np.nanmedian(sglx['bitcode']['bitstart'][()].flatten())\n        vid_file_offset = bitcode_bitstart / fs\n        vidshift = vid_file_offset - bit_start\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n\n    clu_refs = obj['clu'][()].flatten()\n    all_spike_times = []\n    all_spike_trials = []\n    all_qualities = []\n\n    for probe_num in probes:\n        probe_idx = probe_num - 1\n        probe_ref = clu_refs[probe_idx]\n        probe_group = f[probe_ref]\n        quality_refs = probe_group['quality'][()].flatten()\n        trialtm_refs = probe_group['trialtm'][()].flatten()\n        trial_refs = probe_group['trial'][()].flatten()\n\n        for i in range(len(quality_refs)):\n            quality = h5_read_string(f, quality_refs[i]).strip().lower()\n            trialtm = f[trialtm_refs[i]][()].flatten().astype(np.float64)\n            trial = f[trial_refs[i]][()].flatten().astype(np.float64)\n            all_qualities.append(quality)\n            all_spike_times.append(trialtm)\n            all_spike_trials.append(trial)\n\n    # --- traj ---\n    traj_data = None\n    try:\n        traj_refs = obj['traj'][()].flatten()\n        traj_data = {'views': []}\n        for view_idx in range(len(traj_refs)):\n            traj_group = f[traj_refs[view_idx]]\n            ts_refs = traj_group['ts'][()].flatten()\n            ft_refs = traj_group['frameTimes'][()].flatten()\n            feat_names_refs = traj_group['featNames'][()].flatten()\n\n            # Read feat names from first trial\n            feat_refs_trial = f[feat_names_refs[0]][()].flatten()\n            feat_names = [h5_read_string(f, fr) for fr in feat_refs_trial]\n\n            view_trials = []\n            for t in range(min(ntrials, len(ts_refs))):\n                try:\n                    ts = f[ts_refs[t]][()].astype(np.float64)  # (nFeats, 3, nFrames) in HDF5\n                    ft = f[ft_refs[t]][()].flatten().astype(np.float64)\n                    view_trials.append({'ts': ts, 'frameTimes': ft, 'ts_format': 'hdf5'})\n                except Exception:\n                    view_trials.append(None)\n            traj_data['views'].append({'trials': view_trials, 'feat_names': feat_names})\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n\n    f.close()\n\n    return {\n        'bp': bp, 'vidshift': vidshift, 'ntrials': ntrials,\n        'all_spike_times': all_spike_times, 'all_spike_trials': all_spike_trials,\n        'all_qualities': all_qualities, 'traj_data': traj_data,\n        'n_units_raw': len(all_qualities),\n    }\n\n\ndef load_session(anm, date, probes, data_dir_key, params):\n    \"\"\"\n    Load and process one session, following the reference pipeline:\n    loadObjs -> findClusters -> alignSpikes -> getSeq -> removeLowFRClusters\n    Also loads motion energy and computes kinematic features.\n    \"\"\"\n    t0 = time.time()\n    data_dir = DATA_DIRS[data_dir_key]\n    data_fn = os.path.join(data_dir, f'data_structure_{anm}_{date}.mat')\n    me_fn = os.path.join(data_dir, f'motionEnergy_{anm}_{date}.mat')\n\n    session_id = f'{anm}_{date}'\n\n    if not os.path.exists(data_fn):\n        print(f\"  WARNING: {data_fn} not found, skipping\")\n        return None\n\n    # Detect format and load raw data\n    fmt = _detect_file_format(data_fn)\n    try:\n        if fmt == 'hdf5':\n            raw = _load_raw_data_hdf5(data_fn, probes)\n        else:\n            raw = _load_raw_data_v5(data_fn, probes)\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(f\"  WARNING: Could not load {session_id}: {e}\")\n        return None\n\n    bp = raw['bp']\n    ntrials = raw['ntrials']\n    vidshift = raw['vidshift']\n    all_spike_times = raw['all_spike_times']\n    all_spike_trials = raw['all_spike_trials']\n    all_qualities = raw['all_qualities']\n    traj_data = raw['traj_data']\n    n_units_before_quality = raw['n_units_raw']\n    ev = bp['ev']\n\n    # --- Filter clusters by quality ---\n    quality_exclude = params['quality_exclude']\n    keep_mask = np.array([q not in quality_exclude and q != '' and q != 'nan'\n                          for q in all_qualities])\n    good_indices = np.where(keep_mask)[0]\n\n    if len(good_indices) == 0:\n        print(f\"  WARNING: {session_id} has no units after quality filter, skipping\")\n        return None\n\n    # --- Trial filtering ---\n    trial_mask = (bp['early'] == 0) & (bp['stim_enable'] == 0)\n    valid_trials = np.where(trial_mask)[0] + 1  # 1-indexed\n    if len(valid_trials) < 2:\n        print(f\"  WARNING: {session_id} has < 2 valid trials, skipping\")\n        return None\n\n    # --- Align spikes to goCue and bin ---\n    align_times = ev[params['align_event']]\n    edges = np.arange(params['tmin'], params['tmax'] + params['dt'], params['dt'])\n    time_axis = edges[:-1] + params['dt'] / 2\n    n_timebins = len(time_axis)\n    n_valid_trials = len(valid_trials)\n\n    trialdat = np.zeros((len(good_indices), n_timebins, n_valid_trials), dtype=np.float32)\n\n    for neuron_idx, clu_idx in enumerate(good_indices):\n        spike_tm = all_spike_times[clu_idx]\n        spike_trial = all_spike_trials[clu_idx]\n\n        for t_idx, trial_num in enumerate(valid_trials):\n            spk_mask = spike_trial == trial_num\n            if not np.any(spk_mask):\n                continue\n            spk_times = spike_tm[spk_mask] - align_times[trial_num - 1]\n            counts, _ = np.histogram(spk_times, bins=edges)\n            fr = causal_gaussian_smooth(counts.astype(np.float64) / params['dt'],\n                                       params['smooth_window'],\n                                       params['smooth_bctype'])\n            trialdat[neuron_idx, :, t_idx] = fr.astype(np.float32)\n\n    # --- Remove low FR clusters ---\n    mean_fr = np.mean(trialdat, axis=(1, 2))\n    fr_mask = mean_fr > params['low_fr']\n    trialdat = trialdat[fr_mask, :, :]\n    n_neurons = trialdat.shape[0]\n\n    if n_neurons < params['min_units']:\n        print(f\"  WARNING: {session_id} has {n_neurons} units (< {params['min_units']}), skipping\")\n        return None\n\n    # --- Extract trial-level variables ---\n    valid_trial_indices = valid_trials - 1\n    lick_direction = bp['R'][valid_trial_indices].copy()\n    behavioral_context = 1.0 - bp['autowater'][valid_trial_indices]\n    outcome = bp['hit'][valid_trial_indices].copy()\n\n    # --- Load Motion Energy ---\n    me_data = None\n    if os.path.exists(me_fn):\n        try:\n            me_data = _load_motion_energy_generic(me_fn, traj_data, vidshift,\n                                                  align_times, time_axis, ntrials)\n        except Exception as e:\n            print(f\"  WARNING: Could not load motion energy for {session_id}: {e}\")\n\n    # --- Compute tongue and paw velocity from DLC ---\n    tongue_vel = _compute_feature_velocity_generic(\n        traj_data, ntrials, view=2, feat_name='top_tongue',\n        vidshift=vidshift, align_times=align_times,\n        time_axis=time_axis, is_tongue=True)\n\n    paw_vel = _compute_feature_velocity_generic(\n        traj_data, ntrials, view=2, feat_name='top_paw',\n        vidshift=vidshift, align_times=align_times,\n        time_axis=time_axis, is_tongue=False)\n\n    # --- Subsample to valid trials ---\n    valid_0idx = valid_trial_indices  # 0-indexed\n\n    if tongue_vel is not None:\n        tongue_vel = tongue_vel[:, valid_0idx]\n    if paw_vel is not None:\n        paw_vel = paw_vel[:, valid_0idx]\n    if me_data is not None:\n        me_data = me_data[:, valid_0idx]\n\n    # --- Discretize continuous outputs (50th percentile per session) ---\n    tongue_vel_disc = _discretize_velocity(tongue_vel, n_timebins, n_valid_trials)\n    paw_vel_disc = _discretize_velocity(paw_vel, n_timebins, n_valid_trials)\n    me_disc = _discretize_velocity(me_data, n_timebins, n_valid_trials)\n\n    elapsed = time.time() - t0\n    print(f\"  {session_id}: {n_neurons} neurons, {n_valid_trials} trials, \"\n          f\"{n_units_before_quality} raw units -> {int(keep_mask.sum())} after quality -> \"\n          f\"{n_neurons} after FR filter ({elapsed:.1f}s)\")\n\n    return {\n        'session_id': session_id,\n        'animal': anm,\n        'date': date,\n        'n_neurons': n_neurons,\n        'n_trials': n_valid_trials,\n        'time_axis': time_axis,\n        'trialdat': trialdat,  # (n_neurons, n_timebins, n_trials)\n        'lick_direction': lick_direction,\n        'behavioral_context': behavioral_context,\n        'outcome': outcome,\n        'tongue_vel_disc': tongue_vel_disc,  # (n_timebins, n_trials)\n        'paw_vel_disc': paw_vel_disc,\n        'me_disc': me_disc,\n        'tongue_vel_raw': tongue_vel,\n        'paw_vel_raw': paw_vel,\n        'me_raw': me_data,\n    }\n\n\ndef _load_motion_energy_generic(me_fn, traj_data, vidshift, align_times, time_axis, ntrials):\n    \"\"\"Load motion energy and align to neural time axis following loadMotionEnergy.m\"\"\"\n    import scipy.io as sio\n\n    me_cell = None\n    try:\n        me_file = sio.loadmat(me_fn, squeeze_me=True)\n        me_struct = me_file['me']\n        me_cell = me_struct['data'].item()\n    except Exception:\n        me_h5 = h5py.File(me_fn, 'r')\n        me_grp = me_h5['me']\n        me_data_refs = me_grp['data'][()].flatten()\n        me_cell = [me_h5[ref][()].flatten().astype(np.float64) for ref in me_data_refs]\n        me_h5.close()\n\n    side_cam = traj_data['views'][0] if traj_data is not None else None\n    n_time = len(time_axis)\n    me_aligned = np.full((n_time, ntrials), np.nan, dtype=np.float32)\n\n    for trix in range(ntrials):\n        try:\n            me_trial = me_cell[trix].flatten().astype(np.float64) if hasattr(me_cell[trix], 'flatten') else np.array([float(me_cell[trix])])\n        except (IndexError, TypeError):\n            continue\n        if me_trial.size == 0:\n            continue\n\n        ft = None\n        if side_cam is not None and trix < len(side_cam['trials']) and side_cam['trials'][trix] is not None:\n            ft = side_cam['trials'][trix]['frameTimes']\n        if ft is None or ft.size == 0 or np.all(np.isnan(ft)):\n            ft = np.arange(1, me_trial.size + 1) / 400.0\n\n        ft_aligned = ft - vidshift - align_times[trix]\n        min_len = min(len(ft_aligned), len(me_trial))\n        ft_aligned, me_trial = ft_aligned[:min_len], me_trial[:min_len]\n        valid = ~np.isnan(ft_aligned) & ~np.isnan(me_trial)\n        if valid.sum() < 2:\n            continue\n        try:\n            me_aligned[:, trix] = interp1d(ft_aligned[valid], me_trial[valid],\n                                           kind='linear', bounds_error=False,\n                                           fill_value=np.nan)(time_axis).astype(np.float32)\n        except Exception:\n            continue\n\n    for trix in range(ntrials):\n        col = me_aligned[:, trix]\n        if not np.isnan(col).all() and np.isnan(col).any():\n            me_aligned[:, trix] = _fill_nearest(col)\n\n    return me_aligned\n\n\ndef _compute_feature_velocity_generic(traj_data, ntrials, view, feat_name, vidshift, align_times, time_axis, is_tongue=False):\n    \"\"\"Compute velocity of a DLC feature from traj_data (format-agnostic).\"\"\"\n    n_time = len(time_axis)\n    speed = np.full((n_time, ntrials), np.nan, dtype=np.float32)\n\n    if traj_data is None:\n        return None\n\n    view_idx = view - 1\n    if view_idx >= len(traj_data['views']):\n        return None\n\n    view_data = traj_data['views'][view_idx]\n    feat_names = view_data['feat_names']\n\n    feat_idx = None\n    for idx, fn in enumerate(feat_names):\n        if fn == feat_name:\n            feat_idx = idx\n            break\n    if feat_idx is None:\n        for idx, fn in enumerate(feat_names):\n            if feat_name in fn:\n                feat_idx = idx\n                break\n    if feat_idx is None:\n        return None\n\n    for trix in range(min(ntrials, len(view_data['trials']))):\n        trial_info = view_data['trials'][trix]\n        if trial_info is None:\n            continue\n        try:\n            ts = trial_info['ts']\n            ft = trial_info['frameTimes']\n            ts_fmt = trial_info['ts_format']\n\n            if ts.ndim != 3:\n                continue\n\n            if ts_fmt == 'hdf5':\n                x_raw = ts[feat_idx, 0, :]\n                y_raw = ts[feat_idx, 1, :]\n            else:\n                x_raw = ts[:, 0, feat_idx]\n                y_raw = ts[:, 1, feat_idx]\n\n            if ft.size == 0 or np.all(np.isnan(ft)):\n                ft = np.arange(1, len(x_raw) + 1) / 400.0\n\n            ft_aligned = ft - vidshift - align_times[trix]\n            min_len = min(len(ft_aligned), len(x_raw))\n            ft_a, x_r, y_r = ft_aligned[:min_len], x_raw[:min_len], y_raw[:min_len]\n\n            valid = ~np.isnan(ft_a) & ~np.isnan(x_r) & ~np.isnan(y_r)\n            if valid.sum() < 2:\n                continue\n\n            xpos = interp1d(ft_a[valid], x_r[valid], kind='linear',\n                            bounds_error=False, fill_value=np.nan)(time_axis)\n            ypos = interp1d(ft_a[valid], y_r[valid], kind='linear',\n                            bounds_error=False, fill_value=np.nan)(time_axis)\n\n            if not is_tongue:\n                xpos = _fill_nearest(xpos)\n                ypos = _fill_nearest(ypos)\n\n            xvel = np.gradient(xpos)\n            yvel = np.gradient(ypos)\n\n            if is_tongue:\n                xvel[np.isnan(xvel)] = 0\n                yvel[np.isnan(yvel)] = 0\n            else:\n                base_xvel = np.nanmedian(np.diff(xpos))\n                base_yvel = np.nanmedian(np.diff(ypos))\n                xvel -= (base_xvel if not np.isnan(base_xvel) else 0)\n                yvel -= (base_yvel if not np.isnan(base_yvel) else 0)\n                xvel = _fill_nearest(xvel)\n                yvel = _fill_nearest(yvel)\n\n            speed[:, trix] = np.sqrt(xvel**2 + yvel**2).astype(np.float32)\n        except Exception:\n            continue\n\n    return speed\n\n\ndef _fill_nearest(arr):\n    \"\"\"Fill NaN values with nearest non-NaN value.\"\"\"\n    nans = np.isnan(arr)\n    if not nans.any():\n        return arr\n    if nans.all():\n        return arr\n    valid_idx = np.where(~nans)[0]\n    nan_idx = np.where(nans)[0]\n    nearest = np.searchsorted(valid_idx, nan_idx).clip(0, len(valid_idx) - 1)\n    arr[nans] = arr[valid_idx[nearest]]\n    return arr\n\n\ndef _discretize_velocity(data, n_timebins, n_trials):\n    \"\"\"Discretize continuous data into 2 bins using 50th percentile per session.\"\"\"\n    if data is None:\n        return np.zeros((n_timebins, n_trials), dtype=np.int64)\n\n    # Compute 50th percentile across all valid (non-NaN) values\n    valid_vals = data[~np.isnan(data)]\n    if valid_vals.size == 0:\n        return np.zeros((n_timebins, n_trials), dtype=np.int64)\n\n    threshold = np.percentile(valid_vals, 50)\n    disc = (data >= threshold).astype(np.int64)\n    # Replace NaN entries with 0\n    disc[np.isnan(data)] = 0\n    return disc\n\n\n# =============================================================================\n# Plotting functions\n# =============================================================================\n\ndef plot_processing(session_data, save_path):\n    \"\"\"Plot processing visualizations for one session.\"\"\"\n    fig, axes = plt.subplots(4, 3, figsize=(20, 16))\n    session_id = session_data['session_id']\n    fig.suptitle(f'Processing: {session_id}', fontsize=14)\n\n    time_axis = session_data['time_axis']\n    trialdat = session_data['trialdat']\n    n_neurons, n_time, n_trials = trialdat.shape\n\n    # Pick a sample trial\n    trial_idx = min(5, n_trials - 1)\n\n    # 1. Neural activity heatmap for sample trial\n    ax = axes[0, 0]\n    vmax = np.percentile(trialdat[:, :, trial_idx], 95)\n    ax.imshow(trialdat[:, :, trial_idx], aspect='auto', cmap='viridis',\n              extent=[time_axis[0], time_axis[-1], n_neurons, 0], vmin=0, vmax=max(vmax, 1))\n    ax.axvline(0, color='r', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)\n    ax.set_title(f'Neural activity (trial {trial_idx})')\n    ax.set_xlabel('Time from goCue (s)')\n    ax.set_ylabel('Neuron')\n\n    # 2. Mean firing rate across trials for a few neurons\n    ax = axes[0, 1]\n    for i in range(min(5, n_neurons)):\n        ax.plot(time_axis, np.mean(trialdat[i, :, :], axis=1), alpha=0.7)\n    ax.axvline(0, color='r', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)\n    ax.set_title('Mean FR (sample neurons)')\n    ax.set_xlabel('Time from goCue (s)')\n    ax.set_ylabel('FR (Hz)')\n\n    # 3. FR distribution\n    ax = axes[0, 2]\n    mean_frs = np.mean(trialdat, axis=(1, 2))\n    ax.hist(mean_frs, bins=30)\n    ax.axvline(PARAMS['low_fr'], color='r', linestyle='--')\n    ax.set_title(f'Mean FR distribution (n={n_neurons})')\n    ax.set_xlabel('Mean FR (Hz)')\n\n    # 4. Output distributions\n    ax = axes[1, 0]\n    labels = ['Lick Dir', 'Context', 'Outcome']\n    vals = [session_data['lick_direction'], session_data['behavioral_context'], session_data['outcome']]\n    for i, (label, v) in enumerate(zip(labels, vals)):\n        frac1 = np.mean(v)\n        ax.bar(i, frac1, label=f'{label} (frac=1: {frac1:.2f})')\n    ax.set_xticks(range(3))\n    ax.set_xticklabels(labels, rotation=45)\n    ax.set_title('Per-trial output fractions')\n    ax.set_ylabel('Fraction = 1')\n\n    # 5. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Bn7q7NyQPfwP2mrpvbES99","type":"tool_result","content":"     1→Task-switching behavioral paradigm\n     2→\n     3→We designed a behavioral paradigm associated with multiple cognitive processes. In this paradigm, head-fixed mice performed two directional licking tasks that alternated block-wise within each behavioral session. These tasks varied in their cognitive demands but required the same instructed motor output.\n     4→\n     5→This paradigm included an established delayed-response (DR) task in which motor planning is temporally dissociated from movement execution (Fig. 1a). In the DR task, an auditory stimulus indicated the location of a reward. After a brief delay epoch with no auditory stimuli, a separate auditory ‘go cue’ instructed the mouse to move. If the mouse performed a directional tongue movement to the correct target, a water reward was delivered. In separate blocks of trials, mice performed a water-cued (WC) task in which all auditory stimuli were omitted. Instead, a drop of water was presented at a random point in time at a randomly selected reward port. Animals consumed water upon its presentation. Mice received no explicit cues signaling DR and WC blocks. The DR task required a perceptual decision that guides the planning of a subsequent motor action. In the WC task, uncertainty in the timing and location of reward prevented formation of a motor plan before reward presentation, and, instead, mice detected reward availability using olfactory and/or vibrissal cues. This structure required animals to maintain an internal representation of the current block identity (context) to maintain high task performance.\n     6→\n     7→We examined uninstructed movements in this behavioral paradigm using high-speed video. We tracked movement of the tongue, jaw, nose and paws and calculated instantaneous motion energy to quantify movement in a feature-agnostic manner (Fig. 1d–f). We found that mice performed uninstructed movements that varied in their identity and timing across both trials and contexts (Fig. 1e and Supplementary Movie 1).\n     8→\n     9→To assess cortical involvement in instructed movements (directional licking) in both behavioral tasks, we used optogenetic photoinactivation to inhibit the ALM and tjM1 at the go cue (DR) or water presentation (WC) bilaterally in VGAT-ChR2-EYFP mice (10 sessions, four mice). Simultaneous photoinactivation of both regions at the go cue (DR task) or water drop (WC task) impaired the initiation of movement in both contexts (Fig. 1b,c; all DR trials: 41 ± 20% reduction, mean ± s.d., P = 1 × 10−4; all WC trials: 15 ± 20%, P = 0.04; and Extended Data Fig. 1c,d). To assess cortical involvement in the expression of uninstructed movements, and whether these movements might be controlled by ALM or tjM1 preferentially, we bilaterally silenced the ALM or tjM1 individually during the delay epoch of DR trials (ALM: 15 sessions, tjM1: nine sessions, four mice). Uninstructed movements were suppressed by photoinactivation of either area (Extended Data Fig. 1b; ALM: 53 ± 31% reduction, mean ± s.d., P = 3 × 10−4; tjM1: 62 ± 24% reduction, P = 2 × 10−3, paired t-test) and more strongly suppressed by concurrent photoinactivation of both areas (Fig. 1g,h; 29 sessions, four mice; 73 ± 35% reduction, mean ± s.d., P = 7 × 10−9, paired t-test), similar to previous observations21 (but see ref. 34). In the DR task, delay photoinactivation of both areas led to a significant decrease in overall performance (Fig. 1i; 22% ± 14% reduction, mean ± s.d., P = 2 × 10−6 paired t-test; Extended Data Fig. 1b) as expected from the disruption of choice/planning dynamics, often leading to animals responding consistently to a preferred side rather than in a manner commensurate with the sensory cue. These results indicate that both the ALM and tjM1 are involved in the generation of uninstructed movements and the planning and execution of instructed directional tongue movements in the two-context paradigm.\n    10→\n    11→Neural dynamics related to task variables\n    12→\n    13→While movement-related and task-related information is encoded in both the ALM and tjM1 in the DR task and other directional licking tasks33, task variables are more strongly represented in the ALM33,36, and so we focused our subsequent analyses there. We recorded activity extracellularly in the ALM with high-density silicon probes during the two-context paradigm to track dynamics associated with planning, context and the execution of movements (Fig. 2; two-context paradigm: 12 sessions, six mice, 522 units, including 214 well-isolated single units; an additional three mice were trained only on the DR task: 25 sessions, nine mice, 1,651 units, including 483 well-isolated single units; see Extended Data Fig. 2a for per-session statistics). In the DR task, we found that choice selectivity (right versus left DR trials) was widespread across all task epochs as expected (sample: 36%; delay: 42%; response: 58% of 483 single units; 25 sessions, nine mice). Individual units showed a variety of activity patterns across trial types, including delay epoch preparatory activity, which has often been taken to be a neural signature of motor planning32,37 (Fig. 2b, left). Individual units were also selective for behavioral context during all task epochs, including during the inter-trial interval (ITI) (39% of single units, 12 sessions, six mice, 214 single units), suggesting persistent coding of context (Fig. 2b, right).\n    14→\n    15→Methods\n    16→\n    17→Mouse behavior\n    18→\n    19→Behavioral training was conducted using custom scripts written for Bpod r0.5 (https://www.sanworks.io/shop/products.php?productFamily=bpod). All mice used in experiments were first trained on the DR task with a fixed delay epoch until they reached at least 70% accuracy. At the beginning of each trial, one of two auditory tones lasting 1.3 s was played; the tone indicating a ‘right’ trial was white noise, and the tone indicating a ‘left’ trial was a pure tone (8-kHz pulses). The delay epoch (0.9 s for 12 mice, 0.7 s for one mouse and linearly time warped to 0.9 s) started after the completion of the sample tone. After the delay epoch, an auditory go cue was played (swept-frequency cosine (chirp), 10 ms), after which animals were rewarded with approximately 3 µl of water for contacting the correct lickport. Lickport contacts before the response epoch resulted in the current task epoch restarting, ensuring that they could not progress to the next task epoch until they had stopped licking for the specified length of the current epoch. If the animal did not respond within 3 s of the go cue, this was considered an ‘ignore’ trial, although responses were typically registered within 300 ms of the go cue.\n    20→\n    21→Mice used for the two-context task (Figs. 1, 2, 4 and 8 and Extended Data Figs. 1–3 and 9) were introduced to the WC context after they were fully trained on the DR context and at least 2 d before the first electrophysiology recording session. A behavioral session began with approximately 100 DR trials and was then followed by alternating blocks of WC and DR trials. Each interleaved block was 10–25 trials, with no fixed block duration. All sessions started with DR trials. Pilot sessions beginning with WC trials had to be terminated early due to a high ‘ignore’ rate, likely due to the mouse becoming sated early in the session. In a WC trial, all auditory cues were omitted, and an approximately 3-µl water reward was presented randomly from either lickport. Trials in which the animal contacted the lickport before the reward (‘early lick’) were omitted from analyses. ITIs were randomly drawn from an exponential distribution with mean 1.5 s. There were no explicit cues during the ITI to indicate to the animal which context block it was in.\n    22→\n    23→For the randomized delay task (Fig. 3g,h,i), mice were first fully trained on the fixed delay DR task (delay duration of 0.9 s). The delay epoch length was then randomized; the duration for each trial was randomly selected from six possible values (0.3 s, 0.6 s, 1.2 s, 1.8 s, 2.4 s and 3.6 s). The probability of each delay duration being selected was assigned such that it resembled a probability density function of an exponential distribution with τ = 0.9 s, as in ref. 44. Animals were trained on this version of the task until they became experts (>70% accuracy and <20% early lick rate).\n    24→\n    25→Videography analysis\n    26→\n    27→High-speed video was captured (400-Hz frame rate) from two cameras (FLIR, Blackfly monochrome camera, BFS-U3-16S2M-CS). One provided a side view of the mouse, and the other provided a bottom view. We tracked the movements of specific body features using DeepLabCut (Figs. 1, 3 and 4). The tongue, jaw and nose were tracked using both cameras, whereas the paws were tracked using only the bottom view. Position and velocity of each tracked feature was calculated from each camera. The x and y position of each kinematic feature was extracted from the output of DeepLabCut. Missing values were filled in with the nearest available value for all features, except for the tongue. The velocity of each feature was then calculated as the first-order derivative of the position vector. Tongue angle and length were found using the bottom camera. Tongue angle was defined as the angle between the vector pointing from the jaw to the tip of the tongue and the vector defining the direction the mouse was facing. Tongue length was calculated as the Euclidean distance from the jaw to the tip of the tongue.\n    28→\n    29→Motion energy\n    30→\n    31→The motion energy for a given frame and pixel was defined as the absolute value of the difference between the median value of the pixel across the next five frames (12.5 ms) and the median value of the pixel across the previous five frames (12.5 ms). Motion energy for each frame was then converted to a single value by taking the 99th percentile (~700 pixels) of motion energy values across the frame. Motion energy calculated in this manner was high during overt movements over small regions of pixel space, such as during whisking, while remaining relatively low during passive respiration that corresponded to subtle motion across the animal’s body. A threshold above which an animal was classed as moving was defined on a per-session basis manually. Motion energy distributions, per session, were bimodal, showing a large peak with little variance at low motion energy values and a second, smaller peak with high variance at large values. The threshold was set as the motion energy value separating these two modes. We found that this method of setting the threshold captured both short-duration and long-duration movements. Alternative methods, such as defining a baseline period of no movement against which to compare, were less successful due to the variability in timing of the movements across trials.\n    32→\n    33→Photoinactivation experiments\n    34→\n    35→Optogenetic photoinactivation was deployed on approximately 30% of trials selected at random. A ‘masking flash’ (470-mm LEDs; LUXEON Rebel LED) controlled by an Arduino Teensy microcontroller (100-ms pulses at 10 Hz) was delivered constantly for the duration of the session to prevent mice from differentiating control and photoinactivation trials. A 488-nm laser (Coherent, OBIS 488-nm LX 150-mW laser system) was used for all photoinactivation experiments. ChR2-assisted photoinactivation (Fig. 1b,c,g and Extended Data Fig. 1b–d) was performed through a cranial window (see ‘Surgical procedures’ subsection), which replaced bone over the frontal cortex. Light was delivered either at the start of the delay epoch or at the start of the response epoch (only one epoch tested per session). A power density of 1.5 mW mm−2 was used for all photoinactivation experiments.\n    36→\n    37→For delay epoch photoinactivation (Fig. 1g–i and Extended Data Fig. 1b), light was delivered at the onset of the delay epoch and lasted for 0.6 s, followed by a 0.2-s linear ramp down. We targeted one of three regions per session: bilateral motor cortex (ALM and tjM1), bilateral ALM or bilateral tjM1. In this paradigm, head-fixed mice performed two directional licking tasks that alternated block-wise within each behavioral session. These tasks varied in their cognitive demands but required the same instructed motor output.\n\nThis paradigm included an established delayed-response (DR) task in which motor planning is temporally dissociated from movement execution (Fig. 1a). In the DR task, an auditory stimulus indicated the location of a reward. After a brief delay epoch with no auditory stimuli, a separate auditory ‘go cue’ instructed the mouse to move. If the mouse performed a directional tongue movement to the correct target, a water reward was delivered. In separate blocks of trials, mice performed a water-cued (WC) task in which all auditory stimuli were omitted. Instead, a drop of water was presented at a random point in time at a randomly selected reward port. Animals consumed water upon its presentation. Mice received no explicit cues signaling DR and WC blocks. The DR task required a perceptual decision that guides the planning of a subsequent motor action. In the WC task, uncertainty in the timing and location of reward prevented formation of a motor plan before reward presentation, and, instead, mice detected reward availability using olfactory and/or vibrissal cues. This structure required animals to maintain an internal representation of the current block identity (context) to maintain high task performance.\n\nWe examined uninstructed movements in this behavioral paradigm using high-speed video. We tracked movement of the tongue, jaw, nose and paws and calculated instantaneous motion energy to quantify movement in a feature-agnostic manner (Fig. 1d–f). We found that mice performed uninstructed movements that varied in their identity and timing across both trials and contexts (Fig. 1e and Supplementary Movie 1).\n\nTo assess cortical involvement in instructed movements (directional licking) in both behavioral tasks, we used optogenetic photoinactivation to inhibit the ALM and tjM1 at the go cue (DR) or water presentation (WC) bilaterally in VGAT-ChR2-EYFP mice (10 sessions, four mice). Simultaneous photoinactivation of both regions at the go cue (DR task) or water drop (WC task) impaired the initiation of movement in both contexts (Fig. 1b,c; all DR trials: 41 ± 20% reduction, mean ± s.d., P = 1 × 10−4; all WC trials: 15 ± 20%, P = 0.04; and Extended Data Fig. 1c,d). To assess cortical involvement in the expression of uninstructed movements, and whether these movements might be controlled by ALM or tjM1 preferentially, we bilaterally silenced the ALM or tjM1 individually during the delay epoch of DR trials (ALM: 15 sessions, tjM1: nine sessions, four mice). Uninstructed movements were suppressed by photoinactivation of either area (Extended Data Fig. 1b; ALM: 53 ± 31% reduction, mean ± s.d., P = 3 × 10−4; tjM1: 62 ± 24% reduction, P = 2 × 10−3, paired t-test) and more strongly suppressed by concurrent photoinactivation of both areas (Fig. 1g,h; 29 sessions, four mice; 73 ± 35% reduction, mean ± s.d., P = 7 × 10−9, paired t-test), similar to previous observations21 (but see ref. 34). In the DR task, delay photoinactivation of both areas led to a significant decrease in overall performance (Fig. 1i; 22% ± 14% reduction, mean ± s.d., P = 2 × 10−6 paired t-test; Extended Data Fig. 1b) as expected from the disruption of choice/planning dynamics, often leading to animals responding consistently to a preferred side rather than in a manner commensurate with the sensory cue. These results indicate that both the ALM and tjM1 are involved in the generation of uninstructed movements and the planning and execution of instructed directional tongue movements in the two-context paradigm.\n\nNeural dynamics related to task variables\n\nWhile movement-related and task-related information is encoded in both the ALM and tjM1 in the DR task and other directional licking tasks33, task variables are more strongly represented in the ALM33,36, and so we focused our subsequent analyses there. We recorded activity extracellularly in the ALM with high-density silicon probes during the two-context paradigm to track dynamics associated with planning, context and the execution of movements (Fig. 2; two-context paradigm: 12 sessions, six mice, 522 units, including 214 well-isolated single units; an additional three mice were trained only on the DR task: 25 sessions, nine mice, 1,651 units, including 483 well-isolated single units; see Extended Data Fig. 2a for per-session statistics). In the DR task, we found that choice selectivity (right versus left DR trials) was widespread across all task epochs as expected (sample: 36%; delay: 42%; response: 58% of 483 single units; 25 sessions, nine mice). Individual units showed a variety of activity patterns across trial types, including delay epoch preparatory activity, which has often been taken to be a neural signature of motor planning32,37 (Fig. 2b, left). Individual units were also selective for behavioral context during all task epochs, including during the inter-trial interval (ITI) (39% of single units, 12 sessions, six mice, 214 single units), suggesting persistent coding of context (Fig. 2b, right).\n\nMethods\n\nMouse behavior\n\nBehavioral training was conducted using custom scripts written for Bpod r0.5 (https://www.sanworks.io/shop/products.php?productFamily=bpod). All mice used in experiments were first trained on the DR task with a fixed delay epoch until they reached at least 70% accuracy. At the beginning of each trial, one of two auditory tones lasting 1.3 s was played; the tone indicating a ‘right’ trial was white noise, and the tone indicating a ‘left’ trial was a pure tone (8-kHz pulses). The delay epoch (0.9 s for 12 mice, 0.7 s for one mouse and linearly time warped to 0.9 s) started after the completion of the sample tone. After the delay epoch, an auditory go cue was played (swept-frequency cosine (chirp), 10 ms), after which animals were rewarded with approximately 3 µl of water for contacting the correct lickport. Lickport contacts before the response epoch resulted in the current task epoch restarting, ensuring that they could not progress to the next task epoch until they had stopped licking for the specified length of the current epoch. If the animal did not respond within 3 s of the go cue, this was considered an ‘ignore’ trial, although responses were typically registered within 300 ms of the go cue.\n\nMice used for the two-context task (Figs. 1, 2, 4 and 8 and Extended Data Figs. 1–3 and 9) were introduced to the WC context after they were fully trained on the DR context and at least 2 d before the first electrophysiology recording session. A behavioral session began with approximately 100 DR trials and was then followed by alternating blocks of WC and DR trials. Each interleaved block was 10–25 trials, with no fixed block duration. All sessions started with DR trials. Pilot sessions beginning with WC trials had to be terminated early due to a high ‘ignore’ rate, likely due to the mouse becoming sated early in the session. In a WC trial, all auditory cues were omitted, and an approximately 3-µl water reward was presented randomly from either lickport. Trials in which the animal contacted the lickport before the reward (‘early lick’) were omitted from analyses. ITIs were randomly drawn from an exponential distribution with mean 1.5 s. There were no explicit cues during the ITI to indicate to the animal which context block it was in.\n\nFor the randomized delay task (Fig. 3g,h,i), mice were first fully trained on the fixed delay DR task (delay duration of 0.9 s). The delay epoch length was then randomized; the duration for each trial was randomly selected from six possible values (0.3 s, 0.6 s, 1.2 s, 1.8 s, 2.4 s and 3.6 s). The probability of each delay duration being selected was assigned such that it resembled a probability density function of an exponential distribution with τ = 0.9 s, as in ref. 44. Animals were trained on this version of the task until they became experts (>70% accuracy and <20% early lick rate).\n\nVideography analysis\n\nHigh-speed video was captured (400-Hz frame rate) from two cameras (FLIR, Blackfly monochrome camera, BFS-U3-16S2M-CS). One provided a side view of the mouse, and the other provided a bottom view. We tracked the movements of specific body features using DeepLabCut (Figs. 1, 3 and 4). The tongue, jaw and nose were tracked using both cameras, whereas the paws were tracked using only the bottom view. Position and velocity of each tracked feature was calculated from each camera. The x and y position of each kinematic feature was extracted from the output of DeepLabCut. Missing values were filled in with the nearest available value for all features, except for the tongue. The velocity of each feature was then calculated as the first-order derivative of the position vector. Tongue angle and length were found using the bottom camera. Tongue angle was defined as the angle between the vector pointing from the jaw to the tip of the tongue and the vector defining the direction the mouse was facing. Tongue length was calculated as the Euclidean distance from the jaw to the tip of the tongue.\n\nMotion energy\n\nThe motion energy for a given frame and pixel was defined as the absolute value of the difference between the median value of the pixel across the next five frames (12.5 ms) and the median value of the pixel across the previous five frames (12.5 ms). Motion energy for each frame was then converted to a single value by taking the 99th percentile (~700 pixels) of motion energy values across the frame. Motion energy calculated in this manner was high during overt movements over small regions of pixel space, such as during whisking, while remaining relatively low during passive respiration that corresponded to subtle motion across the animal’s body. A threshold above which an animal was classed as moving was defined on a per-session basis manually. Motion energy distributions, per session, were bimodal, showing a large peak with little variance at low motion energy values and a second, smaller peak with high variance at large values. The threshold was set as the motion energy value separating these two modes. We found that this method of setting the threshold captured both short-duration and long-duration movements. Alternative methods, such as defining a baseline period of no movement against which to compare, were less successful due to the variability in timing of the movements across trials.\n\nPhotoinactivation experiments\n\nOptogenetic photoinactivation was deployed on approximately 30% of trials selected at random. signed time from alignment event to start of trial in seconds, None if N/A\\n        'off_end': float or None, # signed time from alignment event to end of trial in seconds, None if N/A\\n        ...\\n    }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n### Key Format Requirements\\n\\n- **neural**: Neural activity data (e.g., firing rates, spike counts) organized by session and trial\\n  - Dimensions: (n_neurons, n_timepoints) for each trial.\\n  - Time bins should be the same size for all trials and sessions. \\n  - There needs to be at least two trials within each session in order to evaluate the decoder performance.\\n\\n- **input**: Variables that serve as inputs **to the decoder**\\n  - These are **decoder inputs**. They could be task inputs to the animal, but inputs to the animal can also be decoder outputs.\\n  - Examples: time from an aligning signal, stimulus characteristics, our animal behavior such as:\\n    - visual: contrast, position, orientation\\n    - audio: frequency, amplitude\\n    - behavior: running speed, pupil size\\n  - Dimensions: (d_input, n_timepoints) for each trial. \\n  - Should capture all relevant contextual information for the decoder\\n  - If an input is a time such as onset of some stimulus, represent it as a binary time series. \\n\\n- **output**: Variables to be decoded/predicted from neural activity\\n  - These are what we want the decoder to **predict**. They could be the animal's output behavior or properties of the stimulus.\\n  - Output variables must be **categorical**, i.e. discrete rather than continuous. If a variable is not discrete, follow instructions from Decoder Task to discretize it. \\n  - Examples: stimulus properties (contrast, orientation), choice (left/right), reaction time, position\\n  - Can be time-varying or discrete values per trial. If at all possible, make it time-varying\\n  - If an output is a time such as when a behavior occurred, represent it as a binary time series. \\n\\n- **subjects**: List of names of all unique subjects (mice).\\n- **subject_idx**: Index into subjects for each session.\\n  - Order should match order of sessions in `neural`, etc.\\n\\n- **brain_regions**: List of names of all brain regions recorded from.\\n- **brain_region_idx**: Index into brain_regions for each neuron in each session.\\n\\n- **input_names**: Names of each input variable.\\n  - Order should match order of `input` dimensions. \\n\\n- **output_names**: Names of each output variable.\\n  - Order should match order of `output` dimensions.\\n- **output_values**: Names of each output value for each output variable.\\n  - Order should match categorical `output` values.\\n\\n- **metadata**: Descriptive information. \\n  - `task_description`: Concise description of the task\\n  - `temporal_alignment_event`: Concise description of temporal alignment event\\n  - `off_start`: Signed time from alignment event to start of trial. Negative means before event, positive after. \\n  - `off_end`: Signed time from alignment event to end of trial\\n  - Add other relevant fields, e.g. `session_info`\\n\\n## Python environment\\n\\n- All required Python packages are already installed in the system Python environment.\\n- Use `python3` to run any python code.\\n- If you need to install additional libraries, use `pip install`.\\n\\n## Decoder Reference\\n\\n- Run this script with `python train_decoder.py <data_file_path>` to validate.\\n- Optional arguments:\\n  - `--verify-only`: Only verify data format and print summary, then exit (does not train decoder).\\n  - `--plot-samples`: Plot sample trials from data and save to png files.\\n  - `--cpu`: Force torch to use CPU only (use if GPU runs out of memory).\\n- Pipe the output to the designated file so that the user can examine it.\\n\\n### Purpose\\n\\nThese functions will be used during the validation phase to ensure:\\n1. Data structure is correct - will report errors and warnings to stdout. \\n2. Dimensions are consistent - will report errors and warnings to stdout. \\n3. Values are sensible - will report errors and warnings to stdout. \\n4. Decoder can successfully train and predict\\n5. Poor performance indicates data formatting issues that need investigation\\n\\n### Consistency requirements\\n\\nYour processing and formatting must **match the reference paper and code** with respect to:\\n- Loading of data\\n- Temporal alignment of different time series streams (neural, inputs, outputs)\\n- Processing of neural, input, and output data streams\\n- Curation of data: filtering of low-quality neurons, trials, sessions, and mice.\\n\\nTo check consistency, you must compare statistics available in the reference paper and your converted dataset. \\n\\nWhenever possible, invent **SANITY CHECKS** that your loading and processing matches the reference paper and code. \\n\\nDiscrepancies are only allowed if required by the Decoder Input and Decoder Output specifications above. \\n\\nCarefully verify your work after every step. When you find mistakes, document and fix them immediately. Be critical of results **after every step of processing**. \\n\\nYou will be assessed on whether the decisions you make on how to load, filter, process, align, reformat, and save the data are reasonable and match the reference paper and code and these instructions. During testing, the reference version of `train_decoder.py` will be run on your converted data. Data statistics and decoder accuracy will be compared to those achieved by human-written conversion code. \\n\\n---\\n\\n## Conversion Workflow\\n\\n**IMPORTANT**: Follow these steps in order. Each step has explicit completion criteria. Do not proceed to the next step until the current step is complete. Any information about dataset size (number of neurons, subjects, sessions, trials)\\n  - Fraction of data with different values, e.g. fraction of rewarded outcomes\\n  - Data processing, curation, and filtering\\n  - Variables important to experiments\\n  - Temporal alignment\\n  - Temporal binning\\n- Read the reference paper to find information about expected decoder accuracy.\\n\\n**Done when**: You have documented expected dataset statistics and processing details in CONVERSION_NOTES.md under \\\"Step 3\\\".\\n\\n**⚠️ CHECKPOINT**: Before proceeding to Step 4, update Step 3 CONVERSION_NOTES.md.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Step 4: Check for Consistency\\n\\n**Goal**: Verify your understanding is consistent across all sources. \\n\\n**Actions**:\\n- Compare your understanding of:\\n  - Important functions from exploring the reference code\\n  - Dataset structure from exploring the dataset\\n  - Analysis described in the reference texts\\n- Note and investigate any discrepancies\\n- In particular, look for discrepancies in:\\n  - Experimental and behavioral variables\\n  - Data processing\\n  - Data curation\\n- Iterate until your understanding of the reference code, dataset, and reference texts are consistent\\n\\n**Done when**: You have resolved all discrepancies and documented your final understanding in CONVERSION_NOTES.md under \\\"Step 4\\\".\\n\\n**⚠️ CHECKPOINT**: Before proceeding to Step 5, update Step 4 CONVERSION_NOTES.md.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Step 5: Mapping Planning\\n\\n**Goal**: Create a detailed plan for mapping source data to target format.\\n\\n**Actions**:\\n- Map source data elements to target format components:\\n  - (Follow Decoder Task section)\\n  - How to discretize continuous outputs (Follow Decoder Task section)\\n  - Which inputs/outputs should be **time-varying** vs **per-trial** (Follow Decoder Task section)\\n  - How does the reference code load and manipulate this data?\\n  - When possible, import or copy code from the reference code in `code` directory. \\n- Consult CONVERSION_NOTES.md under Steps 1-4 and reference materials to determine:\\n  - Temporal binning for spike rates (if applicable)\\n  - Temporal alignment of trials\\n  - Data filtering and curation rules for neurons, trials, and sessions\\n  - Brain regions recorded from\\n- Mapping should be consistent with CONVERSION_NOTES.md under Steps 1-4.\\n- Check for variables indicating valid data periods — exclude invalid data\\n- Note all decisions, edge cases, and data quality issues\\n- Plan and document **sanity and consistency checks** based on dataset size information from the reference texts, code, and data\\n\\n**Done when**:\\n- You have a complete mapping document in CONVERSION_NOTES.md specifying every source-to-target variable mapping under \\\"Step 5\\\"\\n- You have documented all decisions under \\\"Step 5\\\"\\n- You have documented sanity and consistency checks under \\\"Step 5\\\"\\n\\n**⚠️ CHECKPOINT**: Before proceeding to Step 6, update Step 5 CONVERSION_NOTES.md.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Step 6: Script Development\\n\\n**Goal**: Write the conversion script to `convert_data.py`.\\n\\n**Actions**:\\n- Write all conversion code in the file `convert_data.py`\\n- Script should run as **`python -u convert_data.py <outpicklefile>`**\\n- Include options:\\n  - `--full` (default): Process all sessions\\n  - `--sample`: Process only 2 sessions for testing\\n  - `--show-processing`: Plot visualizations of EVERY processing step for up to 2 sessions. Save plots as `processing_<session_id>.png`.\\n- Reuse code from reference code bases where appropriate\\n- Write efficient code:\\n  - Vectorize loops\\n  - Avoid unnecessary file I/O\\n  - Use parallel processing if beneficial\\n  - Print timing information to find bottlenecks\\n- Plots for `--show-processing` mode should visually convince the user that every step of the conversion is correct.\\n  - There are no temporal misalignments\\n  - Discretization of continuous outputs is correct\\n- Write clear, well-documented functions\\n- Handle missing data appropriately (consult references, use sensible defaults, document)\\n- Validate data shapes and types at each step\\n- Include sanity checks (e.g., trial counts match across arrays)\\n\\n**Done when**: `convert_data.py` exists and runs efficiently without errors.\\n\\n**⚠️ DO NOT PROCEED** to Step 7 until `convert_data.py` exists and you have updated Step 6 in CONVERSION_NOTES.md.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Step 7: Sample Conversion and Validation\\n\\n**Goal**: Validate the conversion on a small sample before processing the full dataset.\\n\\n**Actions**:\\n1. Run `python -u convert_data.py sample_data.pkl --sample --show-processing 2>&1 | tee conversion_sample_out.txt`\\n  a. Verify the sample data structure matches the specification.\\n  b. Check dimensions are consistent across trials/sessions.\\n  c. Check that no data is missed during conversion. \\n  d. Validate that metadata accurately describes the data.\\n2. When you do this, make sure that your estimate accounts for differences in lengths/numbers of trials/sessions. \\n  c. If full conversion time estimate is longer than 15 minutes, speed up the code by writing more efficient code (vectorizing loops, removing unnecessary or redundant computations) and/or including parallel processing. \\n3. Verify no errors reported.\\n  b. Attempt to address any warnings\\n  c. Check input ranges and output value distributions against expectations from reference texts.\\n\\n**Done when**: \\n- `sample_data.pkl` is created and passes manual inspection\\n- `verification_sample_out.txt` is created and passes inspection\\n- Processing plots show no anomalies\\n- Document sample statistics in CONVERSION_NOTES.md under \\\"Step 7\\\"\\n\\n**⚠️ DO NOT PROCEED** to Step 8 until `sample_data.pkl` and `verification_sample_out.txt` files exist, and CONVERSION_NOTES.md Step 7 is filled in. \\n\\n---\\n\\n### Step 8: Sample Decoder Training\\n\\n**Goal**: Verify the decoder runs successfully on sample data.\\n\\n**Actions**:\\n1.
